title: Construction of finite coefficient subrings with p-power intersection of fraction subfields
statement: Let $p$ be prime, $k$ a field of characteristic $p$, and $n,m\geq0$. Let $C$ be a domain equipped with a ring isomorphism $e:C\cong k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]][y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $K$ be a fraction field of $C$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] of characteristic $p$. There exist an index set $I$, subrings $A_i\subseteq C$, and subfields $F_i\subseteq K$ containing the prime field $\mathbf F_p$, such that (1) $C$ is finite as an $A_i$-module for every $i$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; (2) the image of every $A_i$ under $C\to K$ lies in $F_i$; (3) $K^p=\{x^p:x\in K\}\subseteq F_i$ for every $i$; (4) $K^p=\bigcap_i F_i$; (5) for every $i,j$ there exists $l$ with $F_l\subseteq F_i\cap F_j$.

proof.text: Choose a p-basis t_i of k using Field.exists_p_basis. Index the family by finite subsets J of its index set I.

Construct k_J as the subfield closure of k^p together with the basis elements outside J. Construct B_J inside P=k[[x_1,...,x_n]][y_1,...,y_m] with carrier all polynomials whose coefficients are in k_J and whose nonzero coefficients have every x and y exponent divisible by p. Zero and one satisfy this condition. It is preserved by addition and negation. For multiplication expand the polynomial coefficient and then the power-series coefficient as two finite antidiagonal sums. Every summand is in k_J. If the sum is nonzero, some summand is nonzero, hence both its factors have p-divisible exponents, so their sums do too. This proves that B_J is a subring, with precisely the coefficient condition required by powerSeriesRingSubfields.

Give K its P-algebra structure by the composite P -> C -> K using e inverse; IsFractionRing.isFractionRing_iff_of_base_ringEquiv transfers the fraction-ring instance. Let K_J be the subfield closure of the image of B_J in K. Subfield.mem_closure_iff and Subring.closure_eq express its elements as quotients of two images of B_J. If the denominator in B_J is zero, the quotient is zero and can instead be written 0/1. Otherwise this is the exact quotient condition of powerSeriesRingSubfields; conversely such quotients are in the closure by closure under division.

Apply RingTheory.powerSeriesRingSubfields to the constructed k_J, B_J, K_J and the chosen p-basis. This supplies finiteness of P over B_J, containment of K^p in every K_J, equality of their intersection with K^p, and K_(J union Jprime) contained in both K_J and K_Jprime.

Set A_J=e inverse(B_J), the subring comap. Restrict e inverse to a ring equivalence B_J -> A_J. Apply Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv to this equivalence and e inverse to transfer finiteness from B_J -> P to A_J -> C. Every image of a in A_J is in K_J by the quotient representation e(a)/1.

Each K_J contains the prime field: every a in F_p has a pth root in F_p by perfection, and the algebra map sends this root to a root in K; containment of K^p gives the claim. Use Subfield.toIntermediateField to obtain F_J over F_p. Its carrier is unchanged. IntermediateField.coe_iInf turns the set intersection equality into the intermediate-field infimum equality. The union of two finite subsets witnesses downward directedness. Return I prime=Finset I with the constructed A_J and F_J.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_powerSeries_finite_subfield_family
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (k : Type t) [Field k] [CharP k p] (n m : ℕ)
    (C : Type u) [CommRing C] [IsDomain C]
    (e : C ≃+* MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k))
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [CharP K p] [Algebra C K] [IsFractionRing C K] :
    ∃ (ι : Type t) (A : ι → Subring C) (F : ι → IntermediateField (ZMod p) K),
      (∀ i, Module.Finite (A i) C) ∧
      (∀ i (a : A i), algebraMap C K a ∈ F i) ∧
      (∀ i, Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p) ⊆ (F i : Set K)) ∧
      (Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p) =
        ((⨅ i, F i : IntermediateField (ZMod p) K) : Set K)) ∧
      (∀ i j, ∃ l, F l ≤ F i ⊓ F j)
